Action.description:
What a rule does. Text may use {{task.key}}, {{task.title}},
{{task.url}}, {{task.status}}, {{run.state}}, {{pr.number}},
{{pr.title}}, {{pr.url}}, {{record.title}}, {{record.url}},
{{collection.name}}, {{page.title}}, {{page.url}}, {{sheet.title}},
{{sheet.url}}, {{whiteboard.title}}, {{whiteboard.url}}, {{rule.name}}
and {{event}}.

oneOf.description:
Launch an agent on the task (or the matching tasks) with the
project's run defaults. On a pull request with no task, starts a run
in the thread of the run that opened it.

agentProfileId.description:
An agent profile to launch instead of the run defaults: its
harness, model settings, instructions and environment.

environmentId.description: An environment in the project; left out, the project's default.

prompt.description: The prompt, for one task; left out, the launch template's.

oneOf.description: Change a field on the task (or the matching tasks).

field.description:
status (by name), priority, assignee ("me", "none", a handle),
add_label, remove_label, or a custom field as "field:<name>"
(see field_list), whose value is written as task_update takes it.

oneOf.description: Put a notification in people's inboxes.
Post a message in a channel, thread, DM or group, as the maker.

Run any operation the rule's maker could run, as the maker, with
{{variables}} filled into its input's text.

Ask someone in the space, usually an agent, to do something (A2.12):
the prompt is posted as the maker, mentioning them, through the
ordinary send, so they are asked to answer with the maker as the
asker, and chain depth, turn limits and Stop apply as to any mention.
It goes in the conversation given, else as a comment on the task.

ActivityLine.description: One activity as the run view draws it.

AgentTemplateView.description: An agent template, as agent_template_list shows it.

definition.description:
The template: instructions, what it may and must not do, when it
asks a person, a suggested role and its skills. Never an account.

confidence.description:
exact (every amount reported per run) or estimated (some split from a
time window).

runs.description: Runs with usage in the period.

left out.

handoff.description:

on top.

one.

active, push_disabled (pushes stopped after failing; saving the

How a list grouped by a date puts records together: by day, by week

blockedBy.description: Tasks that must be done before this one (keys or IDs).

blocks.description: Tasks that can't start until this one is done.

taskId.description: The task: ID, link, or key such as AWD-12.

What blocks it, each with its status. Tasks in projects you can't
reach are left out.

True when it isn't finished, isn't marked blocked, and everything

previous.description: The other device's version, when two saved at once (kept a day).

savedRevision.description: The revision saved before this edit, if one was: restore it to undo.

The board's change counter after the edit. Pass it as
expectedSceneSeq next time to be told when someone else changed what
you're about to touch.

addressed.description: Addressed to one account (heard whatever it subscribes to).

summary.description: What happened, in a few words.

entry.description:
What to pass as package_preview's and package_install's `entry`:
the package's id, or "id@version" where several versions are
listed.

The package's id, such as "software_team" or "studio.game_studio"
(a broken entry: its file or position).

is (any of the values), isNot, empty, notEmpty, contains (text),
gt, gte, lt, lte (numbers and dates).

What to compare with: option names, "me" or @handles, task keys,
numbers, YYYY-MM-DD dates, true or false. Not for empty and
notEmpty.

A field's type: the one list every record kind, collection and module
manifest names types from (T1.2; `modules::contract::FieldType` is this
type). [`FieldType::ALL`] are the types a field can be made with; the
rest are named by module manifests only, until the field layer stores
them (`FieldType::is_stored`). System types (`FieldType::is_system`)
store nothing: they read the record's own columns.

One of its options, each of a status category ("started",
"completed"...), which lists filter, sort and group by.

The project's labels. Declared by manifests only.
An email address, kept lowercase.
A phone number as written, with its digits compared.
When the record was made (system).
When the record last changed (system).

A button field's button: its label and 1 to 3 steps, each an
operation and its arguments, filled from the record when pressed.

The field to change, by its current name or ID. Left out, `name`
finds it, and a name the collection doesn't have adds a field.

name): `IF({Due} < TODAY(), "Late", {Price} * {Qty})`. & joins text.

Choice and status fields: every option, in order (a status option
with its category). An option keeps its records by name; one left
out is archived, never removed. A status field made without options
gets Not started, In progress and Done.

target.description:
For a new link field: "task", "page", or "record:<collection>" for
the records of one of the project's collections, by name or ID.

For a new field: text, long_text, number, date, single_choice,
multiple_choice, status, person, url, email, phone, checkbox or link;
created_time, edited_time, created_by, edited_by or auto_id, which
show the record's own and take no values; formula, worked out from
the record's other fields (give `formula`); or button, which runs
operations when pressed (give `button`). It never changes.

of a field.

chart.

post.description: Move a task, with its subtasks, to another space. The new task gets the title, description, priority, status and type (matched by name), the assignee if they're in that space, acceptance criteria, labels (by name; missing ones are created there), and every comment quoted with its author and date. The original is archived with its full history and links, and its old key (such as AW-7) opens the new task. Custom field values carry over into a field of the same name and type when they fit there; the rest stay on the original. Call first with preview: true to see what carries over and what needs a choice, then move with its snapshot and one resolution per issue (set it in a target field, or leave it).
